quarterly_data.quarter: Dell press release: Dell Technologies Advances Enterprise Agentic AI from the (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dell announced new Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA platforms: the PowerEdge M9882, packing 256 NVIDIA Vera CPUs into a single 48U rack for agentic workload execution (available Q1 CY27); the PowerEdge R8822, air-cooled two-socket NVIDIA Vera CPU performance for standard 19-inch racks with up to four double-wide GPUs (available this month); the PowerEdge XE9810, which Dell says will be the first to deliver rack-scale inference, with 16 direct-liquid-cooled compute trays powered by Groq 3 Language Processing Units (available Q1 CY27); the Dell Modular Data Center with NVIDIA DSX POD reference design, a containerized AI factory with compute, storage, networking, rack-level power and liquid cooling (available early 2027); Dell Pro Precision with GB10 in a 64GB unified memory configuration (available October 23) and Dell Pro Precision with GB300 on Windows with up to 748GB of coherent memory and 20 petaflops of FP4 compute (coming soon); and NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) platforms on Dell PowerEdge servers (coming soon).
quarterly_data.figure: 256 NVIDIA Vera CPUs in a 48U rack; 16 compute trays of Groq 3 LPUs; M9882 and XE9810 in Q1 CY27

quarterly_data.quarter: Dell press release: Dell Technologies Advances Enterprise Agentic AI from the (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA ecosystem and services: Dell says more than 6,500 customers have adopted the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, up from 5,000 last quarter. Validated software now available on it includes Reflection's Beam open-weight model and the knowledge assistant and agentic AI platform with Mistral; AI observability with Dynatrace and computer vision with Fogsphere follow in Q4 CY26, SUSE Linux in early Q1 CY27, and Dell Managed Services for AI in Q1 CY27; a layered agent-security architecture combines Dell infrastructure, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture and Red Hat AI Factory software. CEO Michael Dell: 'AI infrastructure is no longer a cost center. It's a value creation center. Companies are expanding and reallocating budgets because AI infrastructure drives growth, productivity and competitive advantage.'
quarterly_data.figure: more than 6,500 customers, up from 5,000 last quarter
